# Positive pair endpoints do not supply positive returns or a high-occupation pair sector

29 October 2026. New analytic construction; independent review pending. This is a scoped failure of direct paired-boundary renewal and of bare/near-identity paired truncation. It is NOT a sign-problem hardness theorem or a lower bound on arbitrary canonical, tensor, squeezed-state or correlated-field algorithms.

## 1. Native class and the exact positive endpoint operation

For M sites, fix K>=1 particles of EACH flavor and

`H=b†Tb+c†conjugate(T)c+U sum_i(nb_i-nc_i)^2`, `T>=0`, `U>0`.

All one-body diagonal terms are retained. The q_i^2 operator includes its normal-order linear number term. There is no occupation cutoff or pair-creation term. All fixed-number spaces are finite, with one-flavor dimension `D_(M,K)=binom(K+M-1,M-1)`.

Identify `|n>_b|m>_c` with the matrix unit `|n><m|` on the one-flavor K-particle space. If T_K=dGamma(T), H becomes the positive self-adjoint Hilbert--Schmidt superoperator

`Hcal(A)=T_K A+A T_K+U sum_i[n_i,[n_i,A]]`.             (1)

The map Phi_t=exp(-t Hcal) is completely positive and trace nonincreasing: dephasing is trace preserving, and the other factor is A->exp(-sT_K)A exp(-sT_K) with T_K>=0. Finite-dimensional product convergence suffices. The finite-slice HS formula has Kraus operators Gamma_K(B), and therefore

`F_nm(t)=<n,n|exp(-tH)|m,m>`

`= <n|Phi_t(|m><m|)|n> >=0`.                          (2)

At finite slices it is exactly the Gaussian average of `|<n|Gamma_K(B)|m>|^2`; the finite-K limit preserves positivity. Each column of F has sum at most one. This is a genuine positive endpoint operation, not a claim that its individual permanent amplitudes are supplied efficiently.

Let P be the projector onto the BARE paired vectors |n,n>, and Q=I-P. The full canonical trace is `Z=Tr exp(-beta H)`, whereas the endpoint trace is only

`Z_P=Tr[P exp(-beta H)]=sum_n F_nn(beta)`.

They are different. In the matrix picture Z is the superoperator trace over ALL matrix units, not the trace restricted to diagonal matrix units or a sum of population transition probabilities. A preparation/dressing or discarded-weight theorem is required before using Z_P as Z.

# Root whole review: paired endpoints and collective critical sector

29 October2026. ACCEPTED at the declared mathematical scope.
Reviewed PROOF.md SHA256
51ada7a854046c2bb292d0e2bc41e5090eeac3247bc81d97153a5455903d8ee8,
the full exact consumer, RESULT and ordinary-method comparison.
No frozen producer file was edited or consumer rerun.

I reconstructed the Hilbert--Schmidt vectorization and CP/TNI population
endpoint, Schur/Volterra uniqueness, rational trimer sign, all-M resolvent
perturbation transfer and the1/7868 sub-Markov boundary approximation
bound. The K=1 identity D_U=D_0+2U I transports a negative time interval
to every finite U but gives no U-uniform size lower bound. Literal
boundary coordinates and a nonnegative renewal kernel are load-bearing;
general latent coarse graining is correctly outside the obstruction.

The general fixed-M critical estimates also check: the Robertson bound
at depletion<=N/(8M), the complementary scalar-square estimate, polynomial
sector dimension versus exp(-c sqrtN), and the acquired squeezed-trial
normalization give finite r=1 trace and divergence for every r>1. The
trial exponent is (M+1)/(M+3), with strongly M-dependent constants.
This is not a fixed-density thermodynamic conclusion.

P A0 P=P/M and the square-root split give the paired-mass inequality.
The Gibbs variational entropy bound then makes depletion/K vanish at
fixed M and proves limsup paired Gibbs weight<=1/M. The near-identity
dressing exclusion follows directly by the P measurement. Finally the
ordinary large-U Feshbach resolvent error J_K^3/(2U+z)^2 and positive
pair hopping are properly granted at their occupation-dependent scope.

Accepted: the all-M bounded-range K=1 signed-return obstruction; the
specified positive-boundary approximation bound; and the fixed-M all-K
critical/paired-weight results. Not inferred: computational hardness,
failure of arbitrary positive/coarse-grained/nonrenewal representations,
a useful fixed-density bulk solver, or physical validation. The next
constructive assignment targets a collectively dressed critical operation.
